$comment: This file is the authority boundary. The program reads it; the program does
not contain it. Changing what the assistant may do is an edit to this file
plus the prose it quotes -- it is not a code change.
Every rule carries a `quote` lifted verbatim from `source_document`.
src/policy/authority.py refuses to load this file if any quote is not found
in the prose, so the two cannot drift apart silently. If someone edits the
policy text and forgets this file, the run fails loudly at startup instead
of enforcing a boundary that no longer exists.
any   -- at least one phrase must appear in the normalised text
none  -- no phrase may appear (a veto, evaluated last)
Text is normalised to lowercase, punctuation-stripped, whitespace-collapsed
before matching, so 'Review award' and 'review of the award.' behave alike.
issuing_body: Calder County - Department of Household Services
$comment_resolution_order: Section 2 is a CLOSED list of acts the assistant may perform on its own.
It is checked first, because an act named in section 2 is permitted even
when the case it touches is one on which a section 3 action is also owed.
Section 3 is checked next. Anything matching neither list falls to the
default rule, which is section 6.1: unclear means treat it as section 3.
That makes the boundary DEFAULT-DENY -- silence in the policy is a refusal,

default_rule.quote: Where it is unclear whether an action falls within section 3, it is to be treated as though it does.
default_rule.rationale: The requested action is not among the acts section 2 permits, and no specific section 3 provision names it. Section 6.1 resolves the ambiguity against the assistant.
default_rule.supervisor_action: Decide whether this request falls within section 3. If it does, authorise or refuse it. If it does not, it can be returned to the assistant queue.

interpretation.quote: Where it is unclear whether an action falls within section 3, it is to be treated as though it does.
interpretation.effect_on_engine: Ambiguity resolves to requires_approval. Recorded on every decision as interpretation_applied so a supervisor can see where the assistant was unsure rather than certain.

interpretation.quote: The fact that an action would be convenient, or that a caseworker would probably have approved it, is not relevant to whether approval is required.
interpretation.effect_on_engine: There is no confidence, urgency, convenience or likely-approval input to the authority decision. Urgency from the referring party affects ordering only, never authority.

escalation.quote: Where a referral requests an action falling within section 3, the assistant must not perform the action, must not perform a partial or preparatory version of it, and must escalate.
escalation.effect_on_engine: No effect function is bound for any action kind whose authority is requires_approval, so there is no code path that performs one. `no_preparatory_version` on each restricted rule names the drafting/preparation that is also withheld.

escalation.quote: An escalation must identify the referral, state which provision of section 3 applies, and carry sufficient context for a supervisor to act without re-reading the case from the beginning.
escalation.effect_on_engine: src/escalation.py refuses to emit a packet missing referral identity, provision, or resident context.

escalation.quote: Escalation of one referral must not prevent the assistant from continuing to process the others.
escalation.effect_on_engine: Each referral is processed inside its own failure boundary in src/orchestrator.py. An escalation is an outcome, never an abort.

traceability.quote: Every action taken by an assistant must be recorded in a form that allows a supervisor to reconstruct, after the fact, what was done, in what order, on what information, and what was declined.
traceability.effect_on_engine: Hash-chained append-only JSONL ledger in data/runs/. Every step records inputs, the authority decision, the effect, and declined actions with reasons.

traceability.quote: A record which shows only the assistant's output, and not the steps that produced it, does not satisfy 5.1.
traceability.effect_on_engine: The ledger records plan, authority decision, risk classification, gate outcome and effect as separate entries per step -- not just the triage note that came out of the end.

permitted.label: Read a referral from the overnight queue
permitted.quote: Read a referral from the overnight queue.

permitted.label: Retrieve resident history, household composition and case events
permitted.quote: Retrieve a resident's history, household composition, and case events.
permitted.notes: RETRIEVING household composition is permitted. REVIEWING it in the sense a referral means -- reassessing the award in light of it -- is not; that is caught by 3.1. The `none` veto keeps the two apart.

permitted.label: Draft a triage note for caseworker review
permitted.quote: Draft a triage note for caseworker review. A drafted note is a proposal. It has no effect on the case until a caseworker adopts it.
permitted.notes: The permission is specifically for a note addressed to a CASEWORKER or SUPERVISOR, which has no effect until adopted. A note addressed to the RESIDENT is a communication and is caught by 3.5; the `none` veto stops 2.4 absorbing it.

permitted.label: Record that a referral has been read and triaged
permitted.quote: Record that a referral has been read and triaged.

any: record that a referral has been read
record that this referral has been read

permitted.notes: Deliberately narrow. 2.5 permits recording the ASSISTANT'S OWN handling of the referral. It is not a general permission to write to the resident's record -- 'record change of address' and 'record income change' do not match here and fall to section 3.

permitted.label: Flag a referral for human attention, including as urgent
permitted.quote: Flag a referral for human attention, including flagging it as urgent.
permitted.notes: 'Flag for contact attempt' is permitted: raising the flag is the act, and a human makes the contact. The assistant making the contact itself would be 3.5, which the `none` veto keeps out.

permitted.label: Identify an action it may not take and escalate under section 4
permitted.quote: Identify that a referral requires an action the assistant is not permitted to take, and escalate it under section 4.
permitted.notes: This is the permission that makes refusal itself a legitimate, recordable action rather than a failure.

permitted.label: Hand the referral to a caseworker with established context (safeguarding hand-off)
permitted.quote: Where 3.9 applies, the assistant must hand the referral to a caseworker together with whatever it has already established under section 3.2 of Amendment ACA-2026/2.
permitted.notes: Amendment ACA-2026/2 s.3.2 requires handing the referral to a caseworker together with whatever it has already established. This is an ordinary casework hand-off, not a supervisor escalation under section 4.

restricted.label: Suspension, termination or reinstatement of an award
restricted.quote: Suspension, termination, or reinstatement of an award.
restricted.no_preparatory_version: Do not draft the suspension, stage it, set a review date for it, or write anything to the case that presupposes it. Under 4.1 a prepared suspension is still a suspension.
restricted.supervisor_action: Decide whether the award is to be suspended, terminated or reinstated, and record that decision before anything is applied to the case.
restricted.why_irreversible: A suspension stops money reaching a household on the day it takes effect. The Department can restore the award but cannot undo the interruption.

restricted.label: Any change to payment details, including bank or card details
restricted.quote: Any change to payment details, including bank or card details.

any: change account into which payment is made

restricted.no_preparatory_version: Do not record the proposed account, pre-fill a payment mandate, or note the new details anywhere they could be picked up and applied.
restricted.supervisor_action: Verify the account holder against the resident's identity, then authorise or refuse the change of payment destination.
restricted.why_irreversible: Money sent to the wrong account has left the Department. Redirecting a payment is the single highest-value target for account-takeover fraud in this queue.

restricted.label: Initiation, alteration or cancellation of a payment
restricted.quote: Initiation, alteration, or cancellation of a payment.
restricted.no_preparatory_version: Do not queue, schedule or pre-authorise a payment instruction.
restricted.supervisor_action: Authorise or refuse the payment instruction, having confirmed entitlement and amount.
restricted.why_irreversible: A released payment cannot be recalled by the Department acting alone.

restricted.label: Creating a record asserting a finding of fact about a resident's conduct
restricted.quote: Creation of a record that asserts a finding of fact about a resident's conduct, including any record relating to suspected fraud or misrepresentation.
restricted.no_preparatory_version: Do not restate the allegation in the case record as though it were established. An unqualified note saying 'undeclared employment' IS a finding of fact. Repeat it only as a quoted, attributed, unverified allegation inside the escalation.
restricted.supervisor_action: Decide whether the allegation is to be recorded as a finding, referred for investigation, or dismissed. Only a person may make that finding.
restricted.why_irreversible: A fraud marker on a resident's record follows them through every future assessment and is not undone by deleting the note.

restricted.label: Any change to entitlement, award amount or eligibility status
restricted.quote: Any change to a resident's entitlement, award amount, or eligibility status.
restricted.no_preparatory_version: Do not compute a revised award, write a provisional figure to the case, or amend any field the award calculation reads -- address, income, household members. Under 4.1 a staged recalculation is a change to entitlement.
restricted.supervisor_action: Carry out or authorise the reassessment and record the resulting entitlement decision.
restricted.why_irreversible: An entitlement figure, once written, is the basis of the next payment. A wrong one either underpays a household that needs the money or creates an overpayment the Department will later recover from them.
notes: This is the broadest rule in the file and deliberately so.

A referral asking the Department to 'review' an award is not literally asking for a change -- a review can conclude that nothing changes. But the assistant cannot carry out a review without reassessing entitlement, and section 2 grants no power to reassess anything. That makes it unclear at best, and 6.1 resolves unclear against the assistant.

The same reasoning covers 'record change of address', 'record income change' and 'review household composition'. Each looks administrative. Each writes to a field the award calculation depends on. The data pack's warning that 'a routine-looking request can engage section 3 just as squarely as a dramatic one' is aimed exactly here.

restricted.label: Any communication sent to a resident or third party
restricted.quote: Any communication sent to a resident or to a third party.
restricted.no_preparatory_version: Do not draft resident-facing wording at all. A drafted letter is a preparatory version of sending one, and 4.1 withholds preparatory versions. The permitted alternative is a triage note addressed to the caseworker under 2.4, describing what needs saying without composing it.
restricted.supervisor_action: Approve the content and the sending of any communication to the resident or third party.
restricted.why_irreversible: A statement that has reached a resident cannot be unsaid, and an incorrect one about their money causes immediate harm to their planning.
notes: Section 3.5 restricts communication 'sent'. Drafting is not sending, so a literal reading might allow it.
Two things close that gap. Section 4.1 forbids a partial or preparatory version of a section 3 action. And 6.1 requires the unclear case to be treated as falling within section 3.
So the assistant does not compose resident-facing text. It says what needs to be communicated, in a note to a caseworker, and lets a person write it.

restricted.label: Disclosure of resident information outside the Department
restricted.quote: Disclosure of resident information to any party outside the Department.
restricted.no_preparatory_version: Do not assemble or export the disclosure bundle.
restricted.supervisor_action: Confirm the lawful basis for disclosure and approve or refuse the release.
restricted.why_irreversible: Information that has left the Department cannot be retrieved.

restricted.label: Any action which cannot be reversed by the Department acting alone
restricted.quote: Any action which, once taken, cannot be reversed by the Department acting alone.
restricted.no_preparatory_version: Do not take any step that commits the Department to the outcome.
restricted.supervisor_action: Decide whether the Department accepts an outcome it cannot itself undo.
restricted.notes: A catch-all. It is listed last so a more specific provision is cited where one applies, but it means no irreversible action can escape section 3 merely by being unnamed.

restricted.label: Drafting a triage note concerning a household that includes a person under 18
restricted.quote: Drafting a triage note in respect of a referral concerning a household that includes a person under the age of 18.

any: draft triage note for child in household
drafting a triage note in respect of a referral concerning a household that includes a person under the age of 18

restricted.no_preparatory_version: An assistant may not produce a draft note for such a case at all (Amendment ACA-2026/2 s.2.2). Work already done is preserved and handed to a caseworker under s.3.2.
restricted.supervisor_action: Safeguarding requirement: drafting triage notes concerning households with children under 18 requires caseworker judgement from the outset.
restricted.why_irreversible: Safeguarding determination following review; not subject to local discretion.
restricted.notes: Amendment ACA-2026/2 inserts section 3.9. Where household composition cannot be established, 3.9 is treated as applying in accordance with section 6.1.
